decision: Used Tears of Steel (CC-BY, Blender) instead of the library
why: NAS not reachable from a job; this has a real Dolby AC-3 5.1 release, a stereo mix and dialogue plus score
result: four windows x four source kinds

decision: ViSQOL audio mode (pure-Python port) plus SNR; no PEAQ
why: The C++ ViSQOL needs a Bazel build; GstPEAQ needs GStreamer; the port installs in one command. SNR as a cross-check, not a verdict

decision: Checked the metric's ceiling: identity 4.73, native AAC 320k 4.72
why: A scale that saturates below the candidates would hide differences

decision: First run's fixed +4 dB gain pushed hot clips over 0 dBFS; native encoder read 2.9 dB low. Threw the run away and capped gain so the peak lands at -1 dBFS
why: Neutraliser's peak cap prevents overs; a test that clips measures the wrong thing
evidence: diag output in session; run.py gain_db()

decision: ViSQOL and SNR disagreed on libfdk_aac (fdk lower on ViSQOL, +5 dB on SNR). Added a pass with both signals low-passed at 16 kHz and measured each decode's bandwidth
why: fdk cuts at about 16 kHz, native at about 18; the full-band score charges it. A pass that separates bandwidth from in-band quality was the direct test
result: fdk wins in band by 0.02-0.04 at equal rate, loses the top octave

decision: Scoring pool looked hung at 64/100 (idle workers); it was slow ordered output, not a hang. Added resume anyway and NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=1
why: Reading one process list (0% CPU) was a bad observation; a second look showed workers busy

decision: libfdk_aac: no-go. Headroom on native: go as a separate task. E-AC-3: no change
why: Unavailable in shipped image and not redistributable from Debian; in-band gain small and noisy at equal rate; headroom positive in 16 of 16 pairs
